_comment: Curated layer for the `surface` section of docs/capabilities.json (discoverability-design.md §1.2). NOTE the honest boundary: stapel-currencies' capabilities.json is otherwise still HAND-WRITTEN (git log: authored for the stapel-catalog sweep) — provides/axes/extension_points/operations_total are not derived from code here. `make contract` patches in the two derivable things: module/version from pyproject and the derived `surface`. Converting the rest of the document to an emitter is separate work.

convert.intent: Convert a Decimal amount between two active currencies via the base-currency cross rate, quantized to CONVERSION_DECIMAL_PLACES (ROUND_HALF_UP). Call this instead of reading Currency.value rows and dividing/multiplying by hand — the base-currency short-circuit, the active-currency check and the rounding rule are each an easy place to drift from the framework's answer.
instead_of: Currency.value ratio computed and rounded by hand

get_rate_provider.intent: Instantiate the configured STAPEL_CURRENCIES['RATE_PROVIDER'] (validated as a RateProvider subclass). Reach for this instead of resolving/import_string-ing the setting yourself whenever you need today's rates without persisting them — e.g. a preview endpoint that shows what update_exchange_rates would change.

update_exchange_rates.intent: Fetch rates from the configured RATE_PROVIDER and update the Currency rows in one call — the same seam the Celery task and the update_exchange_rates management command already use. Call it from your own scheduler or admin action instead of re-implementing the fetch-then-save loop.
